_comment: Spell ids with NO icon on db.ascension.gg. A CoA ability with no art MAY be unimplemented, cut, or a leftover database row -- but the sample says treat that as a reason to check, never as a verdict: of six flagged interrupts that were checked in game, five were real.
_method: tools/fetch_spell_icons.py harvests the `g_spells` map from each db.ascension.gg spell page; that map carries art for every spell a page references, so an id still unresolved after its own page was fetched has none. Checked only the abilities that appear in notes/raid-utility.md.
_refresh: Re-run the check in tools/utility_tables.py --icons, then re-run the generator. Confirmed-in-game ids should be DELETED from `ids` with a note in `confirmed_present`.

_confirmed_note: Checked in game 2026-08-02. Of the six interrupts flagged for having no icon, five ARE present and only Wrist Snap is not -- so a missing icon is a HINT, roughly 1-in-6 here, not a verdict.

confirmed_absent.800383: Wrist Snap, Barbarian -- confirmed NOT in the game 2026-08-02

_two_signals: There are now TWO independent signals and they are not the same thing. `ids` below means NO ART on db.ascension.gg. `absent_from_ascension` means that database has no record of the spell AT ALL -- the 43-byte `registerSpell(id, 0, {})` response -- which is the stronger of the two. A spell can have a record and no art (12 of these do), which is much weaker evidence than having no record. Note that HTTP 404 on a spell page is NOT absence: 23 ids 404 and 11 of them return complete data from the tooltip endpoint.
_absence_is_not_proof: Three ids are absent from db.ascension.gg entirely AND confirmed in game by a person on 2026-08-02: 500148 Solar Burn, 560470 Distracto Shot, 560471 Hellgaze. So even the stronger signal is a hint. Nothing here justifies removing a row; only `confirmed_absent` does, and that requires somebody logging in.
